/entries/e_jewels/desc: They can express rank or affection, but can also become burdens or gifts that must be returned.
/entries/e_goldchain/desc: A piece of jewelry Clara asks her mother to find for the King, transformed in a letter into an imagined visit inside a painting.
/entries/e_goldchain/archive/0/fields/1/: The King of Spain admires Clara’s chain, and she asks her mother to find another like it
/entries/e_goldchain/archive/0/fields/2/: Her mother turns the search into a fantasy of entering a painting at midnight, making an errand into an entertaining story
/entries/e_goldchain/archive/0/fields/3/: Entering the canvas is literary invention within a letter, not an extraordinary journey she actually makes
/entries/e_letters/desc: Letters between Peru and Spain: witty observations, demands too difficult to bear face to face, and a late generosity.
/entries/e_letters/archive/0/fields/1/la: The coast from which they are sent
/entries/e_letters/archive/0/fields/2/te: She hopes her wit and observations will make Clara smile and offer a little more closeness and appreciation
/entries/e_letters/archive/0/fields/3/te: Her daughter often only glances through them. The son-in-law who admires the writing plays a crucial part in their preservation
/entries/e_letters/archive/0/fields/4/te: The writer calls Letter LVI her first, meaning a new beginning in her attitude
/entries/e_letters/archive/1/fields/2/te: The letters record other lives too; the Captain’s loss of his daughter makes the mother think of her own attachment
/entries/e_letters/archive/1/fields/3/te: However well written, the letters cannot instantly repair their relationship, but preserve the real wishes and changes of that time
/entries/e_letters/archive/1/fields/4/te: The girl’s appeal at the inn was torn up. It must not be treated as a complete document the friar later recovered
/entries/e_porridge/desc: The Marquesa’s usual food. Pepita takes particular care to explain its preparation to the inn’s cook.
/entries/e_charcoal/desc: Fuel needed to warm the mountain room. Tending the brazier is one of Pepita’s daily tasks.
/entries/e_secretletters/desc: Private letters Camila dictates to Manuel, addressed to other people and to be kept secret.
/entries/e_secretletters/archive/0/field: The actress also writes to a bullfighter; affection and reproaches alike are set down by a hired copyist
She forbids him to reveal the contents, even to his twin brother
Dictation close to his ear looks intimate, but does not make the writer the object of the letters’ love
/entries/e_scripts/desc: Spanish plays to copy, memorize and rehearse, connecting the brothers’ labor to the actress’s craft.
/entries/e_scripts/archive/0/fields/0/la: Other writing that must remain secret
/entries/e_scripts/archive/0/fields/1/te: The brothers copy actors’ parts for companies, notices for merchants and music for choirs
/entries/e_scripts/archive/0/fields/2/te: Weary of copying, they turn to loading cargo at the shore and also try cart-driving and ferry work
/entries/e_scripts/archive/0/fields/3/la: Unable to settle at the desk
/entries/e_scripts/archive/0/fields/3/te: After his brother dies, the survivor cannot face sitting quietly to copy and wants work at sea to fill every day
/entries/e_scripts/archive/1/fields/0/la: The teacher who points out details
/entries/e_scripts/archive/1/fields/1/te: Several new plays may be staged in a week, requiring the actors to memorize long, ornate speeches
/entries/e_scripts/archive/1/fields/2/te: Many plays center on male heroes; the actress increasingly finds the women’s parts inadequate
/entries/e_scripts/archive/1/fields/3/te: Teacher and pupil can debate the pace of one speech until dawn and share awe at performing for a poet’s descendant
/entries/e_medicine/desc: Remedies prescribed by a barber-surgeon, which fail to improve Manuel’s wound and illness.
/entries/e_cloth/desc: The dressing the doctor orders changed hourly: something the caregiver dares not stop and the patient dreads.
/entries/e_cloth/archive/0/fields/1/text: The barber-surgeon orders cold applications every hour; the caregiver is reluctant to disobey
/entries/e_cloth/archive/0/fields/2/text: Each application is the patient’s worst moment, and fever and pain make him cry out hurtful words
/entries/e_cloth/archive/0/fields/3/text: When lucid, the patient asks him to continue; his brother longs to skip even one application and give him relief
/entries/e_crucifix/desc: Ill in bed, Manuel swears upon it as he retracts the words with which his pain has wounded his brother.
/entries/e_coin/desc: A copyist’s fee or a child’s pocket money: the same object has a different weight in different relationships.
/entries/e_gift/desc: The present Esteban hopes to buy before leaving, on behalf of his dead brother too. The specific object is never named.
/entries/e_gift/archive/0/fields/1/text: He remembers that she too has lost someone and wants to do something for her before his voyage
/entries/e_gift/archive/0/fields/2/text: He wants the gift to come from both brothers, but struggles to speak the dead brother’s name again
/entries/e_gift/archive/0/fields/3/text: The Captain agrees to choose it together in the morning. The novel does not specify an object subsequently bought
/entries/e_shawl/desc: Pio and Camila once used it to bundle their clothes on tour, a witness to the poverty of those journeys.
/entries/e_mirror/desc: An actress’s everyday tool, reflecting weariness, hope after illness and a gaze she did not expect.
/entries/e_mirror/archive/0/fields/1/tex: When the performing expression falls away, weariness and dissatisfaction emerge on the quiet face
/entries/e_mirror/archive/0/fields/2/tex: She tries powder and cream to disguise her changed face, briefly hoping her stage experience can still help
/entries/e_mirror/archive/0/fields/3/tex: The unexpected visitor appears in the mirror before she can hide even her secret hope
/entries/e_stone/desc: The little object Jaime’s mother gives him to look at on sleepless nights. The novel does not identify its material.
/entries/e_stone/archive/0/title: Something to look at when sleepless
/entries/e_stone/archive/0/fields/1/text: His mother gives it to him at departure, for the nights when he cannot sleep
/entries/e_stone/archive/0/fields/2/text: The novel does not name the stone’s material or give it powers of prophecy or protection
/entries/e_stone/archive/0/fields/3/text: His mother cannot remove his frailty, but tries to leave him something to look at through unfamiliar nights
/entries/e_loneliness/desc: Even in crowds, families and splendid rooms, a person may find no one to whom it feels safe to speak.
/entries/e_obedience/desc: A girl used to following instructions may find it hard to know when she is allowed to leave her post.
/entries/e_courage/desc: A girl uses the word to judge her appeal for help; a mother hears it and begins to reconsider how she loves.
/entries/e_courage/archive/0/fields/1/te: She calls her appeal insufficiently brave, takes it back to her room and tears it up
/entries/e_courage/archive/0/fields/2/te: Hearing the word, the Marquesa looks back at how she has demanded love and decides to write anew
/entries/e_courage/archive/0/fields/3/te: The girl’s self-demand and its effect on the mother can coexist; suppressing a plea for help need not be praised
/entries/e_language/desc: The language the brothers invent as children and use between themselves, made difficult to speak by outsiders’ curiosity.
/entries/e_language/archive/0/fields/1/t: They invent it as they learn to speak; it is more than substituting a few words for Spanish
/entries/e_language/archive/0/fields/2/t: Usually only in private, though urgency sometimes brings a whispered phrase before others
/entries/e_language/archive/0/fields/3/t: Even answering simple vocabulary questions embarrasses them deeply; the recorder finally sees that rank alone is not the cause
/entries/e_applause/desc: It can honor skill or encourage cruelty. An audience’s enthusiasm does not guarantee a performer’s satisfaction.
/entries/e_respectability/desc: The social position Camila seeks after leaving the theatre, bringing new thresholds without ending old unease.
/entries/e_respectability/archive/0/fiel: The home of her new life
She attends fashionable Masses, university ceremonies and charitable occasions, seeking recognized status for her children
She begins to call acting a diversion and gradually restricts her former teacher’s public and private visits
Higher social standing does not teach her how to find peace within her own days
/entries/e_providence/desc: The design Juniper tries to prove by inquiry. Characters understand it differently; the facts do not settle the question.
/entries/e_providence/archive/0/fields/1: His moral scoring during a plague produces the opposite of his expected result, and he eventually tears up the record
/entries/e_providence/archive/0/fields/2: Different relationships bring different accounts; even those closest to the dead may not speak without reserve
/entries/e_providence/archive/0/fields/3: Details of five lives can be discovered without declaring their deaths a punishment or a reward
/entries/e_care/desc: When people cannot take away one another’s pain, staying, bringing water and preparing food remain possible.
/entries/e_care/archive/0/fields/1/text: Pio notices that the jolting ride hurts him and carries him on his shoulder instead
/entries/e_care/archive/0/fields/2/text: Another person’s boundaries do not automatically disappear because a caregiver means well
/entries/e_care/archive/0/fields/3/text: Water, company, food and arrangements in the wards continue to connect those who are alive
